findings.name: reporting-api
findings.root_cause: reporting-api requests 300m CPU / 256Mi memory but observed usage is ~0m CPU and ~3Mi memory (p95), so nearly the entire request sits idle at an estimated $7.69/month.
findings.fix: Lower reporting-api container requests to about 10m CPU and 8Mi memory (≈2x p95 usage); re-measure after a longer window before going lower.

diagnosis.summary: Rightsize audit of analytics: reporting-api is clearly over-provisioned (requests 300m/256Mi vs ~0m/3Mi p95, ~$7.69/mo idle) — recommend cutting to ~10m/8Mi. cache also has idle requests (10m/8Mi vs ~0m/3Mi) but only ~$0.25/mo, not material. ingest-worker was left alone: it runs pinned at its 50m CPU limit (throttled, needs more, not less). Note: the sampling window was short (~2 min, few samples), so confidence is medium; re-verify on a longer window before applying."

findings.name: cache

findings.fix: Remove or correct the nodeSelector on Deployment cache (change disktype: nvme to disktype: standard, or drop it) so the pod matches the existing node; alternatively add an nvme-disk node to the cluster.

diagnosis.summary: The cache deployment's single pod is stuck Pending with FailedScheduling: its nodeSelector disktype=nvme does not match the only node (disktype=standard), so no node is available. Root cause is the nodeSelector in Deployment cache.

findings.name: billing
findings.root_cause: The billing container uses envFrom on ConfigMap "billing-config", which does not exist in the namespace, so kubelet cannot build the container config and the pod stays Pending with CreateContainerConfigError.
findings.fix: Create the missing ConfigMap billing-config in namespace billing (or remove the envFrom reference from the billing Deployment), then let the pod restart.

diagnosis.summary: billing pod is stuck in Pending with CreateContainerConfigError: its container's envFrom references ConfigMap "billing-config" which does not exist in namespace billing (only kube-root-ca.crt exists). Root cause is the missing ConfigMap; fix by creating it or removing the envFrom reference from the billing Deployment.

findings.name: defaults
findings.root_cause: statement-builder sets no memory limit, so the namespace LimitRange "defaults" injects a 32Mi default limit (16Mi request); the workload's ~50MB in-memory build exceeds that injected limit and is OOMKilled (exit 137), crash-looping.
findings.fix: Set an explicit memory limit on statement-builder large enough for its build (e.g. >=256Mi) so it is not capped by the LimitRange 32Mi default; alternatively raise the LimitRange default if 32Mi is too small for this namespace.

diagnosis.summary: statement-builder has no memory limit in its Deployment, but the finance namespace LimitRange "defaults" applies a 32Mi default memory limit (16Mi request). The container loads ~50MB into memory, exceeds the injected 32Mi limit, and is repeatedly OOMKilled (exit 137, 3 restarts), leaving the Deployment with 0 ready replicas. Fix: set an explicit adequate memory limit on the workload (or raise the LimitRange default).

findings.name: defaults
findings.root_cause: statement-builder sets no memory limit, so the finance LimitRange 'defaults' injects a 32Mi default; the job loads ~50MB of ledger rows into memory and is OOMKilled (exit 137) on every start, crash-looping the pod.
findings.fix: Set an explicit memory request/limit on the statement-builder Deployment container large enough for its working set (e.g. 128Mi limit), overriding the 32Mi LimitRange default.

diagnosis.summary: statement-builder in finance is OOMKilled (exit 137, 3 restarts). The Deployment sets no memory limits, but the namespace LimitRange 'defaults' applies a 32Mi default limit / 16Mi request to containers without one. The workload loads ~50MB of data into memory, exceeding the injected 32Mi limit, so it is killed each start. Fix: give the container an explicit memory limit above its working set (or raise the LimitRange default).

findings.name: thumbnailer
findings.root_cause: The log-shipper sidecar cannot reach its upstream collector, so it buffers 4Mi log batches in the shared emptyDir /buffer until pod ephemeral storage exceeds the 20Mi limit set on that container; kubelet then evicts the pod and the Deployment recreates it, repeating every few minutes.
findings.fix: Restore connectivity to the upstream log collector so the sidecar stops buffering, and raise the log-shipper ephemeral-storage request/limit above 20Mi (or cap the buffer size).

diagnosis.summary: Thumbnailer pods are repeatedly evicted because the log-shipper sidecar, unable to reach its upstream collector, fills the shared emptyDir /buffer past the 20Mi ephemeral-storage limit on that container. Two consecutive pods (dmsmn, tmnsq) were Evicted with 'ephemeral local storage usage exceeds the total limit of containers 20Mi', and the Deployment keeps recreating them. Fix: restore the upstream collector connection and/or raise the ephemeral-storage limit (or bound the buffer).

findings.name: ledger
findings.root_cause: ledger pod exits with code 2 on every start because its config value "retries" is the string "three" instead of an integer, so the app panics and the Deployment stays at 0/1 ready.
findings.fix: Correct the ledger configuration: set retries to an integer (e.g. 3) in the config source feeding the ledger container, then restart the pod.

findings.name: ledger-api
findings.root_cause: Service ledger-api selects app=ledger-gateway but no pod carries that label (the healthy gateway pod is labeled app=ledger-api), so it has zero endpoints and never answers.
findings.fix: Change the Service selector to app=ledger-api (or add the app=ledger-gateway label to the ledger-api pods) so it matches the running gateway pod.

diagnosis.summary: Two independent root causes break the ledger area. (1) The ledger Deployment crash-loops: its container exits 2 with 'panic: invalid config key \"retries\": expected integer, got \"three\"', so 0/1 replicas are ready. (2) The ledger-api Service is dead-on-arrival: its selector app=ledger-gateway matches no pods (the healthy ledger-api pod is labeled app=ledger-api), giving 0 endpoints, which is why the service does not answer even though its backend pod is Running/Ready."

findings.name: auth-api
findings.root_cause: session-svc proxies /login to https://auth-api and its TLS verification fails with 'certificate has expired', producing 502s; auth-api's serving certificate (CN auth-api, issued by Internal Services CA 2026) expired 2026-09-26, one day before the report.
findings.fix: re-issue the auth-api serving certificate from the Internal Services CA 2026 (current tls.crt expired 2026-09-26) and update the auth-api-tls secret it is served from

diagnosis.summary: Logins 502 through session-svc because upstream auth-api serves an expired TLS cert. session-svc nginx logs: repeated 'upstream SSL certificate verify error: (10:certificate has expired)' on GET /login, each a 502. ConfigMap auth-api-cert/tls.crt (CN auth-api, issuer Internal Services CA 2026) expired 2026-09-26 (-1 day); the CA itself is valid to 2036, so this is leaf expiry, not a trust mismatch. Fix: re-issue the leaf cert and rotate the auth-api-tls secret.

findings.name: stock-db
findings.root_cause: stock-db loads its stock index into memory but the container is capped at a 24Mi memory limit, so it is OOMKilled (exit 137) on every restart and never becomes ready; stock-api repeatedly loses its database and crash-loops with 'database unavailable after 3 attempts'.
findings.fix: Raise the stock-db memory request/limit well above the index size (e.g. 256Mi) in the stock-db Deployment.

findings.name: statement-builder
findings.root_cause: statement-builder buffers ~50MB of ledger rows in memory while its container has a 32Mi memory limit, so it is OOMKilled (exit 137) on every run and the deployment stays at 0/1 ready.
findings.fix: Raise the statement-builder memory limit to cover the working set (e.g. 128Mi) or stream the ledger rows instead of buffering them.
